conclusion: A separate terminal variant may retain the original initial DS4 /bin/sh -i +m boundary and replace only its fixed ENV value plus strictly derived identity environment. A fixed trusted script invokes the native network client as an ordinary foreground child and records its returned status before the shell prompt. This removes client-created descriptor/thread state from the future shell inheritance problem; it does not establish runtime qualification or descendant cleanup after forced termination.

zsh_source.provenance: pinned PureDarwin zsh.nix inherits zsh.src/version; locally acquired5.9.1 archive. Source excerpts read as data, not installed. Candidate must still bind exact selected RAM sh/zsh bytes and applied derivation.

source_findings.fact: Wrapper sets argv0=sh, resolves /private/var/select/sh and execv, then falls back bash/zsh. Candidate must bind exact selector and zsh binary; do not assume every /bin/sh implements the inspected behavior.

PRIVILEGED means differing real/effective UID or GID, not simply UID0. Interactive SH/KSH emulation with PRIVILEGED unset reads ENV; non-login invocation skips /etc/profile and .profile. ENV parsestr/singsub expansion precedes source(); run_init_scripts precedes setupshin and main loop.

try_source_file may prefer SCRIPT.zwc when present and at least as new as text, even when the text is missing. Fixed path/text hash alone is insufficient. Require absent compiled sibling and fixed trusted ancestor/file identity.

source opens script with O_RDONLY|O_NOCTTY, moves it to>=10 marked FDT_INTERNAL, executes a non-top-level source loop, then closes SHIN and restores prior shell input. Normal external-command path closes internal shell descriptors before exec. No source-file FD must be treated as a network leak in the parent while sourcing.

Normal non-final/explicit-exec-free external command forks, parent adds owned child to job table and waits via waitjobs/zwaitjob; SIGCHLD handling performs wait3/waitpid. Put an explicit post-command status assignment/printf after the client; forbid exec, &, pipelines, substitutions and traps in the tiny fixed script. A foreground wait can also stop on an error/stopped job, so require normal exit status and separate child record/prompt predicates.

Original DS4 sets session/ctty/stdio, clears mask and resets CHLD/TERM/PIPE/job-control signals. Keep +m: normal foreground child does not enter the MONITOR setpgrp/attachtty branch and remains in shell session/group. Interactive shell ignores TERM; external child resets TERM/INT/PIPE defaults. No custom SIGCHLD trap, SIG_IGN or background job handling is needed.

Actual Darwin derivation replaces SIGCHLD sigsuspend with zsleep(10000), wait_for_processes(), return-1. The native wait path must be tested; Linux same-version host fixtures do not execute this patch.

Requested AF_INET path issues A-only DNS through shared DNSService connection. getaddrinfo sorting calls si_destination_compare even for AF_INET when comparison is needed. mDNS request loop is synchronous kqueue processing; it closes per-call kqueue and query contexts but normally retains _mdns_sdref. dispatch_once and pthread_atfork alone are not evidence of spawned worker threads.

Address comparison can initialize os_log and a cached PF_SYSTEM netsrc socket; netsrc creation sets O_NONBLOCK without a CLOEXEC assignment on this path. DNSService connection sets CLOEXEC best-effort and logs fcntl failures. DNSServiceSetDispatchQueue is a separate opt-in API, not called by the inspected mdns loop. Whole-library logging/dispatch thread quiescence is not proven, and no fake claim that an async DNS worker necessarily exists is made.

fdt_fork allocates a distinct child descriptor table and references inherited fileglobs; descriptors newly opened by the client cannot appear in its parent shell. Process exit marks workqueue exiting, handles AIO and invalidates open files before workqueue teardown. Exit may block: source does not prove a bounded syscall/termination latency.

narrow_candidate_contract: Create a new source-bound terminal variant only; frontend004 remains unchanged except selecting its existing absolute --terminal binary path. Preserve app002 source and its qualified observations.

Keep initial executable/argv /bin/sh [sh,-i,+m], original DS4 pre-exec FD sweep/check/status EOF convention, stdio and finite PTY owner. ENV must be one constant absolute path with no shell metacharacter expansion. All argv/environment allocations remain before app fork.

Bind fixed source script bytes and native client Mach-O bytes in the new packet. No script symlink/writable component or adjacent .zwc; require exclusive immutable candidate filesystem assumptions. Do not obtain script text/path from CLI, records, arbitrary environment or user configuration.

Only strict identities from /private/var/run/darwin-desktop-network/session-HEX48/INSTANCE48 may enter fixed environment: lowercase hex48, slot0001/0002, instance tail=session prefix44, exact full session from parent basename, checked0700 directories. Native client revalidates. Script quotes every parameter and invokes one fixed absolute client path, never eval/shell -c/background/exec/pipeline/command substitution.

Client records its distinct PID, PPID=shellPID, getsid/getpgrp/tcgetpgrp all matching the retained shell session/group before lookup. Initial client-entry stdio-only fcntl observation, if desired, must precede getaddrinfo and remain entry-only evidence; do not broadly close unknown library FDs or add a pre-second-exec scan.

Client prints bounded early terminal banner, performs ordinary getaddrinfo and sockets with complete own result/raw-byte record, closes its explicitly owned HTTP/record descriptors and exits. Library-owned persistent state ends with that process; do not manually tear down private DNSService/libinfo global state. No later exec of shell.

Shell saves immediate client status then emits a fixed instance/session/shellPID-bound post-client marker and returns to its normal prompt. Success requires matching complete client record, normal return status0, marker after that child return, actual prompt and verified foreground relation. A missing ENV/client still can show prompt and must fail networking qualification.

No claim that a post-client shell has only0/1/2: it legitimately owns its controlling-tty FD/loader state. The original app-private descriptor exclusion remains a pre-initial-exec fact. Real target after-exec properties require their own observations.

Keep the enclosing finite application deadline while DNS may block. Normal child return/reap before prompt provides the success path. If teardown occurs before return, do not infer client reap/absence from killpg or direct shell wait: require separate retained PID/process-start identity evidence or mark descendant cleanup incomplete. Never signal cached client PID after lost ownership/ECHILD. Existing session shutdown continues to reap only its direct shell.

Network service remains alive until terminal/client/frontend completion evidence or explicitly failed bounded cleanup; no client activity may be assumed finished merely from READY, a shell prompt or parent signal success.

focused_tests.scope: Linux same-version zsh host fixture, no Darwin/network/hardware proof

limits: No target shell/Darwin resolver run, runtime FD inventory, network request, boot, SSH or hardware action
Host tests use local ELF zsh5.9.1 with synthetic child/FD worker only; they are not native patched-zsh runtime proof
No forced-grandchild-reap solution is implemented; normal success and interrupted cleanup are separate predicates
No proof of complete libinfo/os_log/dispatch quiescence is needed or claimed under process separation
Source comparisons and tests do not replace exact new packet/source/RAM/script identity checks
contract_refinement: Supersedes only the proposed startup-program-then-second-exec design in the currently frozen desktop-service contract; write a distinct revision rather than changing that original proposal.
